html:
SMTO-EXE-0113 — The browser couldn't open that web page

GUID: 0d127cc4-33bd-500e-a27f-56307b270f13
Slug: browser-navigation-failed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO asked the browser to go to a page, but the page didn't load. The website might still have received the request, so the browser may be on a different page than expected.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO: "Which page is your browser showing now?" Don't ask it to repeat the step yet. The website may have received the request even though the page did not finish loading.
  2. Check the web address SMTO used. Make sure it is spelled correctly and that the site opens for you. A misspelled address or a site that no longer exists is a common reason a page fails to open.
  3. Make sure the computer running the Gateway is online and can reach that website, for example through the same company network or VPN. The page is loaded from the Gateway's computer, not from the device you are using SMTO on.
  4. If the step was a reload or going back after sending a form, check the website to see if the form went through. Ask SMTO to retry only if it didn't. Reloading or going back can send a form a second time.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the page you expected as the current page in its browser.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the web address you wanted, to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't keep asking SMTO to reload a page that sends a form or payment.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A navigate, back, forward or reload operation on the Gateway raised a non-timeout error; effect_unknown records whether the navigation had already been sent.

What this means

  • A navigation operation raised an exception that was not the recognized timeout class; the service retains whether its effect boundary had been crossed. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • A navigation operation raised an exception that was not the recognized timeout class; the service retains whether its effect boundary had been crossed.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect page_info, the requested URL and retained effect facts; the generic category does not establish DNS, server or page-policy cause.

How to fix it

  • BrowserService._execute classified a non-TimeoutError exception from page.goto/go_back/go_forward/reload as navigation_failed (provider text is not exposed); navigation is dispatched before the call, so effect_unknown is normally true. Inspect browser.page_info and the receipt's effect_unknown, confirm the host resolves and is reachable from the Gateway host (DNS, proxy, TLS, firewall), and navigate again only after confirming the earlier request had no unwanted effect.
  • Inspect browser.page_info and the intended URL. Resolve connectivity or page access before navigating again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect browser.page_info and the intended URL. Resolve connectivity or page access before navigating again.

How to verify the fix

  • Current page and external effects are understood before any separately authorized navigation.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
